header.userPrompt:
Feature: merchant names as implicit categorization rules (merchant-alias model), end to end.

Context: rules live in merchant_rule (action set_merchant|ignore, pattern CITEXT, merchant_id). Matching is in lib/api/shared ImportRuleMatcher (normalize = lowercase + strip non-alphanumerics, then substring contains; 3-char normalized floor; longest normalized pattern wins; ignore beats set_merchant) and RowRuleVerdict. Today a merchant only auto-matches a row if an explicit set_merchant rule exists, and the confirm-expense modal (web BankRowCreateExpenseForm) stores the merchant name as the pattern via a "Use original description as rule pattern" checkbox. That denormalizes the name (renaming a merchant leaves the rule stale) and ~60% of rules just duplicate the merchant name; it also silently creates a second overlapping rule when a row already matched one, and swallows rule-creation errors.

Goal: every merchant name matches implicitly; explicit set_merchant rules are only ALIASES for when the bank text differs from the name.

Engine:
1. In lib/api/shared, add one helper that, given explicit rules plus the user's merchants, returns the effective List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]: explicit rules plus one virtual SetMerchant rule per merchant (pattern = merchant name, merchantId = that merchant). Reuse the existing length floor and longest-match/ignore precedence unchanged. Virtual rules are computed, never stored. An explicit rule duplicating a merchant-name virtual rule must not change the winner.
2. Route every merchant/verdict resolution for a row or description through this helper so matching includes merchant names: RowRuleVerdict callers, BankStatementReviewPage, StatementSuggestionsService and JevStatementSuggestionsService (selectRowsToResolve), ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction, TelegramExpenseAction, ParseReceiptAction, ReceiptsPage, ReconciliationMatcher/BankStatementAutoReconcilePage, BulkMerchantSetupPage, and the bank-row forms. Pass merchants where already loaded; load them where not.

UX (web BankRowCreateExpenseForm):
3. Remove the checkbox. The rule concept becomes an alias field shown ONLY when the resolved merchant's normalized name is NOT already a substring of this row's description (implicit matching won't catch future rows). In that case show an editable "Rule pattern" field defaulted to the row description; blank means do not create a rule. When the merchant name already matches the row, show a read-only note that future rows match automatically and create no rule.
4. If the row already matches an existing explicit rule, show it read-only ("Covered by rule: X") and offer no creation.
5. Create a rule only when the field is non-empty and its normalized value differs from the merchant name. Surface rule-creation errors inline instead of swallowing them; the expense must still be created independently of rule success.

Do NOT delete or migrate any existing rules; this PR is additive. Keep behavior identical for rows already matched by an explicit alias or ignore rule. Tests: unit-test the helper (name matches containing description; "CAFE DINDURRA" beats "CAFE"; ignore wins; <3-char names excluded; renamed merchant changes matching with no rule row). Avoid redundant action-level tests the reviewers would flag.

resultJson.description:
Today a bank-statement row or receipt only auto-resolves to a merchant if there is an explicit `set_merchant` row in `merchant_rule`. Because of that, the confirm-expense form (`BankRowCreateExpenseForm`) has been storing the merchant name as a rule pattern. About 60% of rules just repeat a merchant name. They go stale when the merchant is renamed. Overlapping rules get created silently when a row already matched one, and rule-creation errors are swallowed. This epic makes every merchant name an implicit rule: matching runs over the explicit rules plus one computed (never stored) virtual SetMerchant rule per merchant, where the pattern is the merchant name and merchantId is that merchant. Explicit set_merchant rules then only serve as ALIASES for bank text that differs from the merchant name.

The engine stays the same: normalize = lowercase and strip non-alphanumerics, then substring contains; normalized patterns under 3 chars never match; the longest normalized pattern wins, with ties going to the larger UUID string; ignore beats set_merchant. A single shared helper in `lib/api/shared` builds the effective rule list. Every caller that resolves a merchant or verdict for a row, description or receipt vendor (server suggestions services, Telegram, receipt parsing; web review page, bank-row forms, auto-reconcile, bulk setup, receipts) goes through it. When an explicit SetMerchant rule has the same normalized pattern as a merchant name, the explicit rule keeps the decision: the virtual rule for that name is dropped. A duplicate therefore never changes the outcome, and an explicit alias that points elsewhere still wins. Assumption to confirm with the user: longest-match is kept unchanged across explicit and virtual rules. So a merchant name strictly longer than a matching explicit alias (e.g. merchant "Cafe Dindurra" vs alias "CAFE") wins. Rows matched by ignore rules, or by explicit aliases with no longer merchant name in the description, behave exactly as before.

The confirm-expense UX then drops the "Use original description as rule pattern" checkbox:
- If the row already matches an explicit rule, show "Covered by rule: X" and create nothing.
- Else, if the chosen merchant's name already matches the row, show a read-only note that future rows match automatically.
- Otherwise, show an editable "Rule pattern" field that defaults to the row description; blank means no rule.

A rule is created only when the field is non-blank and its normalized value differs from the merchant name. The expense is created first and independently. A rule failure is shown inline in the form instead of being swallowed. The PR is additive: no rules are deleted or migrated, and no DB/schema change is made.

tasks.title: Add ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules (virtual merchant-name rules) with unit tests
tasks.description:
In lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala add `def effectiveRules(explicit: List[Rule], merchants: List[(UUID, String)]): List[Rule]`. It returns the explicit rules plus one virtual `Rule(id = merchantId, ImportRuleAction.SetMerchant, pattern = merchantName, merchantId = Some(merchantId))` per merchant. Skip a merchant whose normalized name equals the normalized pattern of any explicit SetMerchant rule, so the explicit rule decides and a duplicate never changes the winner. Do not filter by length here: findMatches already applies the 3-char floor. Leave findMatches/findWinner/findRowWinner/findReceiptWinner/RowRuleVerdict unchanged. Add a short doc comment saying virtual rules are computed, never stored, and that their id is the merchant id. Tests go in ImportRuleMatcherSpec (subject `"effectiveRules" should`, per RULE-TE-001; don't rename the existing describe blocks), checked via RowRuleVerdict.verdict / findRowWinner / findReceiptWinner on the result. Cover:
- merchant 'Oxxo' matches the description 'OXXO STORE 123' with no explicit rules (SetMerchant(Some(oxxo.id)))
- merchant 'Cafe Dindurra' beats merchant 'Cafe' for 'CAFE DINDURRA MADRID', and also beats an explicit alias 'CAFE' pointing at another merchant
- an explicit Ignore rule wins over a matching merchant name
- a merchant whose normalized name is under 3 chars (e.g. 'A&B' → 'ab') never matches
- after a rename (same id, new name) matching follows the new name with no rule row: old text no longer matches, new text does
- an explicit SetMerchant rule with the same normalized pattern as a merchant name, pointing at a different merchant, still decides the verdict, and a duplicate pointing at the same merchant gives the same verdict as no duplicate
- findReceiptWinner over effective rules resolves a receipt vendor 'MERCADONA, S.A.' to merchant 'Mercadona'

Verify: `sbt "testOnly *ImportRuleMatcherSpec"` (lib/api is cross-built; the JVM test is enough) and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Server: route suggestions, Telegram and receipt parsing through effectiveRules
tasks.description:
Every change goes through ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(explicitRules, merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name)).
(1) StatementSuggestionsService.selectRowsToResolve: add a `merchants: List[Merchant]` parameter and compute the verdict over effective rules, so debit rows whose description contains a merchant name count as rule-skipped and are not sent to the model. Update the call in StatementSuggestionsService.resolve and the one in JevStatementSuggestionsService.resolve; both already have `merchants`. Update the class scaladocs that say 'no import rule' to also cover merchant names.
(2) ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction already loads merchants and passes them through; confirm nothing else is needed and leave it alone.
(3) TelegramExpenseAction: in the `case None` branch (no exact findByName hit), load `merchantsRepository.all(userId)` next to `importRuleRepository.all(userId)` and call findRowWinner on the effective rules. The Ignore/SetMerchant handling and the following flow stay the same.
(4) ParseReceiptAction: load `merchantsRepository.all(doc.userId)` and call findReceiptWinner on the effective rules. Keep the existing fallback that creates a pending merchant and an auto rule unchanged (it is out of scope).

Tests:
- Update existing StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec / JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec calls for the new signature, fixing any fixture whose merchant names now substring-match row descriptions.
- Add ONE selectRowsToResolve case: a debit row whose description contains a merchant name is skipped by rule.
- Do NOT add new TelegramExpenseActionSpec or ParseReceiptActionSpec cases (the helper's unit tests cover the logic). Only fix existing ones that break.

Verify: `sbt "testOnly *StatementSuggestionsServiceSpec *JevStatementSuggestionsServiceSpec *TelegramExpenseActionSpec *ParseReceiptActionSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Web: route BankStatementReviewPage and bank-row forms' matching through effectiveRules
tasks.description:
(1) BankStatementReviewPage: compute the effective rules once with `Hooks.useMemo(() => ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(ruleList, merchantList.map(m => m.id -> m.name)), List(ruleList, merchantList))`. Use them in the rowInfoById memo (rowInfo → verdict/resolveImport), so rows matching a merchant name become Ready / ReviewExpense, and bulk 'Process ready' uses them too. Keep the `ruleList` state as explicit rules only (BankRowCreateExpenseForm needs the explicit list for 'Covered by rule' later). Update the rowInfo/resolveImport scaladoc to say the list they receive is already effective.
(2) Inside BankRowCreateExpenseForm.initialSelection and BankRowCreateRefundForm (matchedMerchant), compute effectiveRules(props.ruleList, merchants) themselves, since both already receive explicit ruleList plus merchants. Keep the Props shapes unchanged.

Tests: update BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec, BankStatementReviewPageSpec and BankStatementReviewRowSpec where fixtures now match implicitly. Example: BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec's row 'OXXO STORE 123' with merchant 'Oxxo' and `Nil` rules now resolves to Oxxo, so give those AI-fallback cases a description that matches no merchant name. Add one initialSelection case: a merchant-name match with no explicit rule is preselected over the AI suggestion. Add one rowInfo/resolveImport case: a row matched only by a merchant name resolves to that merchant and its category.

Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec *BankStatementReviewPageSpec *BankStatementReviewRowSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: Web: route ReconciliationMatcher, AutoReconcile, BulkMerchantSetup and Receipts through effectiveRules
tasks.description:
(1) ReconciliationMatcher (web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/ReconciliationMatcher.scala): add a `merchants: List[GetMerchants.Response.Merchant]` parameter to `reconcile`. Have reconcile and qualifyingCreateRequests both match over ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(rules, merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name)). For a virtual winner, rule.pattern is the merchant name, so the existing name-proxy candidate check works as is; leave that logic alone. Update the callers in BankStatementAutoReconcilePage: the initial useMemo call passes Nil rules today; pass Nil merchants too, keeping today's behavior, and use the loaded merchantList where rules are used.
(2) BulkMerchantSetupPage: the unmatchedGroups filter uses findRowWinner on effective rules (ruleList + merchants state), so descriptions already covered by a merchant name stop showing as unmatched. Leave DescriptionRow's rule creation alone.
(3) ReceiptsPage: both findReceiptWinner calls (batch-confirm resolution around line 502 and single confirm around line 1098) use effective rules built from ruleList + props.merchants.data.

Tests: update ReconciliationMatcherSpec and BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec for the new signature and any fixtures that now match implicitly. Add one ReconciliationMatcherSpec case: with no explicit rules, a row whose description contains a merchant name produces a create request with that merchant's category. No DOM tests.

Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *ReconciliationMatcherSpec *BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

tasks.title: BankRowCreateExpenseForm: replace the checkbox with a conditional alias field and surface rule errors
tasks.description:
Remove the `useDescAsPattern` state and the checkbox UI. Add pure, unit-testable helpers to the BankRowCreateExpenseForm object:

(a) `enum RuleHint { case CoveredByRule(pattern: String); case MatchesByName; case NeedsAlias }`, and `def ruleHint(row, explicitRules: List[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule], merchantName: String): RuleHint`.
- CoveredByRule when ImportRuleMatcher.findRowWinner(explicitRules, row.description) is defined: explicit rules only, any action.
- Else MatchesByName when the merchant name would implicitly match: normalized length >= 3 and normalize(description) contains normalize(name). Reuse ImportRuleMatcher, e.g. `findMatches(List(virtual rule), description).nonEmpty`, rather than re-implementing the floor.
- Else NeedsAlias.

(b) `def aliasToCreate(pattern: String, merchantName: String): Option[String]` gives Some(trimmed) only when the trimmed pattern is non-empty and its normalize() differs from normalize(merchantName).

The merchant name used is the typed merchantInput.trim (the selected merchant's name when one is picked, or the new merchant's name).

UI, below the Category field:
- CoveredByRule: read-only Typography 'Covered by rule: <pattern>'.
- MatchesByName: read-only note, e.g. 'Future rows matching "<name>" are matched automatically'.
- NeedsAlias: an outlined small TextField labelled 'Rule pattern' with state defaulted to props.row.description and a helper text saying blank means no rule.
- Show nothing when the merchant input is empty.

Submit:
1. Reorder so the expense is created first: category → merchant → createExpenseFromRow.
2. Then, only when the hint is NeedsAlias and aliasToCreate(...) is Some and there is a resolved merchant id, call createImportRule(SetMerchant, alias, merchantId). Never wrap it in `.recover { case _ => None }`.
3. Call onNewEntities with the new merchant, and the new rule if one was created, as soon as each exists.
4. If the rule call fails after the expense succeeded, don't call onSuccess yet. Keep the form open in a 'saved' state: an inline error such as 'Expense created, but the rule could not be created: <msg>', with Save disabled or hidden so the expense can't be submitted twice, and a 'Close' button that calls props.onSuccess(expenseId). This keeps the rule error inline and keeps the expense independent of the rule.
5. Expense or merchant failures keep today's setError path.

Keep the Props shape (ruleList = explicit rules). Follow AP-FE-01/02: build elements inside render and use `def` for anything reused.

Tests, pure only (RULE-TE-010, no DOM), in BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec:
- ruleHint returns CoveredByRule when an explicit alias matches (even if the name also matches), MatchesByName when only the name matches, and NeedsAlias when the name doesn't occur in the description and when the name normalizes to under 3 chars
- aliasToCreate returns None for blank/whitespace, None when the alias normalizes to the merchant name (e.g. 'O.X.X.O' vs 'Oxxo'), and Some(trimmed) otherwise

Verify: `sbt "web/testOnly *BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec"` and `CI=true sbt Test/compile`.

resultJson.brief:
MODULES
- lib/api/shared (cross-built JVM + JS): Tapir models plus pure utils used by both server and web. The rule engine lives here.
  - lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/ImportRuleMatcher.scala
    - `case class Rule(id: UUID, action: ImportRuleAction, pattern: String, merchantId: Option[UUID])`
    - `normalize(s) = s.toLowerCase.replaceAll("[^a-z0-9]", "")`
    - `matches(rule, text)`: substring check on normalized values
    - `findMatches(rules, text)`: applies the 3-char normalized floor
    - `findWinner`: longest normalized pattern, ties by larger `id.toString`
    - `findRowWinner(rules, description)`: ignore winner beats set_merchant winner
    - `findReceiptWinner(rules, merchantName)`: SetMerchant rules only
  - lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/RowRuleVerdict.scala
    - `verdict(rules, description): Verdict`, one of NoRule | Ignore | SetMerchant(Option[UUID])
    - `ruleMerchantId(rules, description): Option[UUID]`
  - Tests: lib/api/shared/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/api/utils/{ImportRuleMatcherSpec,RowRuleVerdictSpec}.scala. AnyWordSpec + must Matchers; helpers `setMerchantRule(id, pattern, merchantId)` and `ignoreRule(id, pattern)` already exist in ImportRuleMatcherSpec.
  - Models: `GetMerchants.Response.Merchant(id, name, notes, categoryId, taxId = None, reviewed, createdAt)` and `GetImportRules.Rule(id, action, pattern, merchantId, merchantName, autoCreated, createdAt, updatedAt)`, both in lib/api/shared/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/api/models/merchants/. `ImportRuleAction.{SetMerchant, Ignore}`.
- server/ (Play): controllers → actions → repositories (Anorm). Server merchant model: `net.wiringbits.repositories.models.Merchant(id, userId, name, notes, categoryId, taxId, reviewed, createdAt, updatedAt)`. `MerchantsRepository.all(userId): Future[List[Merchant]]`. `ImportRuleRepository.all(userId)` returns rows convertible with `_.transformInto[ImportRuleMatcher.Rule]` (Chimney), or manually as `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule(r.id, r.action, r.pattern, r.merchantId)`.
- web/ (Scala.js + Slinky + MUI 5): pages in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/, utils in web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/utils/. Pages load explicit rules via `ctx.api.client.getImportRules` and map them to ImportRuleMatcher.Rule; merchants come from `ctx.api.client.getMerchants`.

HELPER DESIGN (decided)
- `ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(explicit: List[Rule], merchants: List[(UUID, String)]): List[Rule]` returns the explicit rules plus one virtual `Rule(id = merchant.id, SetMerchant, pattern = merchant.name, merchantId = Some(merchant.id))` per merchant.
- Drop a virtual rule when an explicit SetMerchant rule has the same normalized pattern: the explicit rule decides, so duplicates never change the outcome.
- Callers pass `merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name)`. The tuple keeps lib/api free of server/web model types.
- The 3-char floor and precedence come from the unchanged findMatches/findWinner/findRowWinner. Don't add another length check.
- Virtual rule ids are merchant ids. Never look up an explicit rule by a winner's id without checking. When code needs "the explicit rule covering this row", call findRowWinner on the explicit list only.
- Compute effective rules once per batch or render (useMemo on web), not per row.
- Pending (unreviewed) merchants are included: `all()` returns them.

CALL SITES
Server:
- services/StatementSuggestionsService.scala: `selectRowsToResolve(rows, rules)` at ~L168 is private[services] and also used by JevStatementSuggestionsService via import. Both `resolve` methods already take `merchants: List[Merchant]`.
- actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsAction.scala already loads merchants and passes them to the service.
- actions/telegram/TelegramExpenseAction.scala: about L36-53. Exact `findByName` runs first, then rules via findRowWinner on the normalized name.
- actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala: about L84-115, findReceiptWinner on the vendor name. MerchantsRepository is already injected; a fallback creates a pending merchant plus an autoCreated rule (leave that as is).

Web:
- BankStatementReviewPage.scala: `resolveImport` (L94-123), `rowInfo` (L138), the `rowInfoById` useMemo (L338), ruleList state (L242, explicit). The form is wired at L828-850; `onNewEntities` appends to ruleList/merchantList and `onSuccess` closes the form and shows a toast.
- BankRowCreateExpenseForm.scala:
  - `initialSelection` (L41) and `isPristine`
  - checkbox state `useDescAsPattern` (L99) and its UI (L426-439)
  - `handleSubmit` (L177-279): today creates the rule BEFORE the expense, with `.recover { case _ => None }`
  - the error Typography pattern at L339
- BankRowCreateRefundForm.scala: L38 uses `RowRuleVerdict.ruleMerchantId(props.ruleList, …)`.
- BankRowRuleForm.scala: only creates rules, no matching changes needed.
- ReconciliationMatcher.scala: `qualifyingCreateRequests(rows, rules, merchants)` and `reconcile(rows, expenses, rules)`. reconcile uses `rule.pattern` as a merchant-name proxy; virtual rules fit that naturally.
- BankStatementAutoReconcilePage.scala L81-137.
- BulkMerchantSetupPage.scala: the L97 `unmatchedGroups` filter. DescriptionRow (L182+) still creates description and merchant-name rules; leave it alone, out of scope.
- ReceiptsPage.scala: L502 and L1098 use findReceiptWinner; merchants are `props.merchants.data`.

CONVENTIONS
- docs/guide/testing.md RULE-TE-001: the should-subject is the method name only, never the class or object name.
- RULE-TE-005: actions are not tested directly, so don't add action specs.
- RULE-TE-010: no new DOM tests. Extract pure functions in the component's object and unit-test them (see BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec, a plain AnyWordSpec with `mustBe`).
- Frontend: no object-level vals holding React elements (AP-FE-01); use `def` for elements reused in one tree (AP-FE-02); prefer theme/CSS vars over hex (AP-FE-03). Form code already uses `e.target.asInstanceOf[dom.HTMLInputElement].value` for TextField onChange; match it.
- CLAUDE.md: no hacks or setTimeout ordering, no silent defaults, surface errors.
- DB: no schema or migration change in this epic; don't delete or migrate rules.
- Build: `CI=true` turns warnings into errors (-Werror). Typecheck with `CI=true sbt Test/compile`. Run targeted tests with `sbt "testOnly *Spec"` (server or lib) or `sbt "web/testOnly *Spec"`. Don't run the full `sbt test` per task. Run `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before finishing.

GOTCHAS
- Existing fixtures may now match implicitly and change expectations. Example: BankRowCreateExpenseFormSpec's row "OXXO STORE 123" with merchant "Oxxo" and `Nil` rules now resolves to Oxxo, so the AI-fallback cases need a description that matches no merchant name. Check BankStatementReviewPageSpec, ReconciliationMatcherSpec, BulkMerchantSetupPageSpec and the StatementSuggestions specs the same way.
- Ignore rules still always win, including over merchant names.
- Longest-match applies across explicit and virtual rules: a longer merchant name beats a shorter explicit alias. This is intended; it is flagged as an assumption in the epic.
- Merchant names can normalize to the same string ("Café" and "Cafe" are both "caf"/"cafe"-style collisions). The tiebreak then goes to the larger merchant UUID, which is acceptable.

findings.title: Unused sbt setting keys in build.sbt

reason.text: Out of scope: this change did not touch build.sbt. These keys (webpackExtraArgs, stMinimize, webpackDevServerPort) are existing configuration that the scalajs-bundler and ScalablyTyped plugins read, and lintUnused itself says a key may still be used. Removing them or excluding them from lint is a separate build cleanup.

reason.text: Out of scope. This branch makes no changes to build.sbt (`git diff main -- build.sbt` is empty). The flagged keys are existing scalajs-bundler and ScalablyTyped configuration (webpackExtraArgs, webpackDevServerPort, stMinimize), which those plugins' tasks and commands such as fastOptJS::startWebpackDevServer read. lintUnused itself says such keys may still be used. The build passes with CI=true, so this is a separate build cleanup, not part of the merchant-rules change.

entries.resultJson:
The full suite now passes. `CI=true NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider sbt test` exited 0, with 832 server tests and 223 web tests passing and no failures in the lib suites.

**What failed on the first run:** 3 tests in `ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec` (829 of 832 server tests passed). This was caused by this branch's own change, not by anything unrelated. The test's sample bank rows `SUPERMART 123` and `UBER TRIP` contain the names of its sample merchants, `SuperMart` and `Uber`. Merchant names now act as implicit rules, so those rows were resolved by rule and never sent to the AI model, which is what the tests check.

**Fix:** a test-only change in `server/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/actions/bankstatements/ResolveStatementSuggestionsActionSpec.scala`. I renamed the two row descriptions to `GROCERY STORE 123` and `RIDE SHARE TRIP`, which match no merchant name, so the AI path is tested again. No production code changed.

**Environment:**
- Postgres was already running in Docker.
- I put Node v24.15.0 on PATH, because the shell's default Node 16 rejects `--openssl-legacy-provider`.
- I ran `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before the final run.

The fix is uncommitted in the working tree.
